kubectl describe pvc clichy-postgres-1 -n clichy-prod

No database backup/restore automation is present in the inspected repository. Retain prevents Kubernetes from automatically deleting PV data on claim release but is not a backup. See backup and restore.

docs.title: Automated deployment
docs.text: Push to master triggers CI, image builds, Test deployment and then Production deployment, as described in CI/CD. Deployment uses exact commit SHA tags. The self-hosted runner must have access to the target K3s kubeconfig, kubectl, Node 24, pnpm, GHCR, and namespace secrets. The script refuses to run unless the cluster reports exactly one node named valtask.

docs.title: Manual checked-out SHA deployment
docs.text:
From a clean checkout that matches the published images:

CLICHY_DEPLOY_CONFIRM=yes ./infra/kubernetes/scripts/deploy.sh test sha-<40-character-commit-sha>
CLICHY_DEPLOY_CONFIRM=yes ./infra/kubernetes/scripts/deploy.sh prod sha-<40-character-commit-sha>

Use manual commands only when the selected image tag exists and git rev-parse HEAD matches it. Production deploy additionally checks required Secret keys and GHCR pull-secret type. The script migrates first, renders manifests into a temporary Kustomize directory, applies the environment, waits for API/web/worker rollouts, and prints workload status. Without CLICHY_DEPLOY_CONFIRM=yes, it asks for interactive confirmation.

docs.title: Before/after checks
docs.text:
kubectl config current-context
kubectl get nodes
./infra/kubernetes/scripts/migrate.sh test status
kubectl get deployments,pods,pvc,ingress -n clichy-test -o wide
kubectl rollout history deployment/clichy-server -n clichy-test

After a failure, inspect kubectl describe, events, Pod logs, migration status, and PostgreSQL logs before retrying. There is no automated rollback step. Do not delete PVCs or reset the database to address rollout failures. A deliberate rollback would need a compatible prior image SHA and an operator review of schema compatibility; the repo does not provide a turnkey rollback script.

docs.title: Known issues and resolved incidents
docs.text: This is a record of issues evidenced by current documentation, source, or Git history. Absence of an open item here does not mean the system has been tested comprehensively.

docs.title: Production database missing Prisma tables
docs.text: Status: Resolved (2026-11-14) Affected component: Production Better Auth / PostgreSQL deployment Symptoms: Account registration returned HTTP 500 and logs reported Prisma P2021, missing public.user. Root cause: The new Production database had not received migrations. Earlier deployment automation migrated Test but not Production. Resolution: Applied pending 20261005225922_adding_photos_objects migration to Production using prisma migrate deploy through a temporary loopback-only port-forward. Registration then worked. Verification: The contemporaneous operations record reports Prisma schema up to date and a successful account creation; this is historical execution evidence, not a current live check. Relevant files: infra/kubernetes/scripts/migrate.sh, infra/kubernetes/scripts/deploy.sh, .github/workflows/ci.yml, packages/db/prisma/migrations/. Related commits: c96c262 (“Fixing migration issue in prod and adding the migration process to ci/cd”), c3624d8 (Production deployment script); detailed incident record was already in docs/operations/known-issues.md before this documentation work.

docs.title: PostgreSQL connectivity and Prisma deployment stability
docs.text: Status: Historical fixes present; current operation unverified Affected component: Prisma, PostgreSQL Service and deployment scripts Symptoms: Commit history records 7e8f334 “fix connectivity issue between prisma and postgresql pod” and 21d2785 “fix: database to prisma connection stability.” Root cause: Not established by commit subjects alone. Current migration script uses a loopback port-forward, dynamically discovers its local port, and validates with a PostgreSQL protocol SELECT 1; exact earlier failure mechanism is not established. Resolution: Connectivity changes and a more defensive migration path are in the current tree. Verification: Source inspection only for this documentation pass. Relevant files: infra/kubernetes/scripts/migrate.sh, packages/db/src/, infra/kubernetes/base/postgres/.

docs.title: Prisma migrations over the CNPG loopback port-forward
docs.text:
Status: Resolved and confirmed by a successful Test workflow.

Symptoms: The migration script's node-postgres SELECT 1 probe succeeded through kubectl port-forward, but Prisma migrate deploy and migrate status returned P1001. The port-forward was reset when Prisma opened its connection.

Cause and resolution: Prisma's PostgreSQL connector defaults to sslmode=prefer; the pg readiness probe does not request TLS for the generated URL. The port-forward URL is loopback-only, so migrate.sh now explicitly sets sslmode=disable when rewriting the temporary URL. This keeps the probe and Prisma on the same protocol. The Kubernetes Secret and application connection URL are not changed. The fix was confirmed by the Test deployment workflow.

Relevant files: infra/kubernetes/scripts/migrate.sh, docs/infrastructure/ci-cd.md. Related commits: 7e8f334, 21d2785.

docs.title: Production CNPG application role mismatch
docs.text:
Status: Resolved; user confirmed the Production database connection and deployment flow work after the Secret reload correction.

Symptoms: Production migrate.sh port-forward failed on its first database connection. The primary Pod remained Running, and the direct local socket query returned pg_is_in_recovery() = false.

Root cause: The CNPG Cluster declares bootstrap.initdb.owner: clichy, but the Production application Secret originally used the PostgreSQL username clichy_prod. After the username was corrected, PostgreSQL still logged SQLSTATE 28P01 with User "clichy" has no password assigned. The Secret referenced by bootstrap.initdb.secret lacked CNPG's cnpg.io/reload: "true" label, so the Secret update did not promptly trigger reconciliation of the role password. The endpoint, primary, and PVCs were healthy; this is a credential synchronization issue, not a storage or port-forward routing failure.

Resolution: prepare-namespace.sh normalizes the local DB URL and POSTGRES_USER to clichy, retaining the current password and database name, and labels clichy-postgres-app with cnpg.io/reload: "true". Apply the label immediately with kubectl label secret clichy-postgres-app -n clichy-prod cnpg.io/reload=true --overwrite; then confirm CNPG synchronizes the password before retrying migrations. Sync the updated script before the next environment preparation so the label persists. Do not delete or recreate the Cluster or its PVCs.

Verification: User confirmed that the corrected Production setup works. A successful migration-status/deployment run is operational evidence for database connectivity; it does not by itself verify physical streaming or failover.

Relevant files: infra/kubernetes/scripts/prepare-namespace.sh, infra/kubernetes/cnpg/cluster.yaml, infra/kubernetes/overlays/prod/database/kustomization.yaml, infra/kubernetes/scripts/migrate.sh.

docs.title: Citus sharding experiment
docs.text: Status: Historical experiment; not operational Affected component: Database architecture Symptoms: Project context supplied for this documentation task reports Citus was experimentally introduced, encountered problems, and was not retained. Root cause: Not verified from current repository or available commit subjects. Resolution: Current architecture is standard PostgreSQL plus Redis/BullMQ; current schema/manifests show no Citus deployment. Verification: Current manifests and package files inspected; a working Citus setup is absent. Relevant files: infra/kubernetes/base/postgres/, packages/db/. Related commits: No Citus-specific commit was identified in current master history search. Treat the experiment history as project-provided context until historical commits/docs are made available.

docs.title: Traefik Ingress routing corrections
docs.text: Status: Historical correction committed; current reachability unverified Affected component: Clichy and Headlamp Ingress Symptoms: Git history records a Traefik port/entrypoint correction and Headlamp Ingress namespace correction. Root cause: Commit message 637e762 says base Ingress did not explicitly select web, and Headlamp Ingress had been declared in default; details beyond that message are not established. Resolution: Base Clichy Ingress explicitly uses entrypoint web; Headlamp Ingress is in headlamp, and installer removes the earlier misplaced resource. Verification: Current manifest/source inspection only. Relevant files: infra/kubernetes/base/ingress.yaml, infra/kubernetes/headlamp/lan-ingress.yaml, infra/kubernetes/scripts/install-headlamp.sh. Related commit: 637e762.

docs.title: PostgreSQL data directory ownership
docs.text: Status: Current fix committed; live storage not verified Affected component: Production PostgreSQL StatefulSet and local PV setup Symptoms: Most recent commit title indicates a permissions issue for PostgreSQL UID 999. Root cause: The commit message establishes that the data directory permissions needed correction for UID 999; exact runtime symptom is not available from repository evidence. Resolution: Current prepare-namespace.sh checks/sets ownership for an empty PostgreSQL directory and 2a7717f adjusts ownership handling. It intentionally refuses unsafe recursive ownership changes on populated data. Verification: Source inspection; not tested against live volume. Relevant files: infra/kubernetes/scripts/prepare-namespace.sh, infra/kubernetes/base/postgres/statefulset.yaml. Related commits: 2a7717f, 4bceaff.

docs.title: Operational gaps (not recorded incidents)
docs.text: These are limitations established by configuration, not claims of past failures: Production CNPG is deployed and healthy, but direct WAL streaming/failover evidence is still outstanding; PostgreSQL sharding is absent, no tested backup/restore runbook exists, Redis is a single instance, and no Test refresh/anonymization procedure exists. See the database pages and requirements matrix.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Start with namespace and context checks to avoid inspecting the wrong cluster:

kubectl config current-context
kubectl get nodes
kubectl get deployments,pods,services,endpoints,pvc,ingress -n clichy-test -o wide
kubectl get events -n clichy-test --sort-by=.lastTimestamp
Symptom Checks Pod pending / PVC pending kubectl describe pod, kubectl describe pvc; verify StorageClass, local PV node affinity and node path. ImagePullBackOff Check image tag and ghcr-pull-secret exists in the workload namespace; never display its data. API can't connect PostgreSQL Check CNPG Cluster Ready status, primary Pod role, clichy-postgres-rw endpoints, DATABASE_URL Secret presence/key name, and namespace match. Use migrate.sh <env> status for a protocol-aware DB check. Migration fails Read workflow/script output and PostgreSQL logs; run migration status; do not reset DB or remove PVC. Upload returns 400/413 Check supported format and 20 MiB multipart cap; image decoder also caps at 40 million pixels. Photo stays pending Inspect worker readiness/logs, Redis connectivity, queue name, outbox rows and photo storage mount. The worker Deployment has no Kubernetes probe despite exposing port 3001. Thumbnail missing Confirm photo belongs to user, processing completed, derivative exists on shared volume, and API/worker mount same PVC. HPA has unknown metrics Inspect HPA events, metrics APIService, kubectl top pods, CPU requests and monitoring separately. Prometheus does not itself guarantee the Kubernetes resource metrics API required by HPA. Ingress unavailable Verify host DNS, Traefik, Ingress class/entrypoint, Service endpoints and whether TLS is configured for that host.

For logs: kubectl logs deployment/clichy-server -n clichy-test, kubectl logs deployment/clichy-worker -n clichy-test, and kubectl logs -l cnpg.io/cluster=clichy-postgres -n clichy-test --all-containers. Use production namespace only with appropriate access and redact user data/secrets from any shared diagnostic output.

For CNPG, inspect kubectl get cluster,pods,pvc -n clichy-test -o wide, kubectl describe cluster clichy-postgres -n clichy-test, and kubectl logs -n cnpg-system deployment/cnpg-controller-manager. kubectl cnpg status is available only if the optional CNPG CLI plugin is installed. Check separate PVC binding, disk space, UID 26 ownership on Prod local PV paths, and Prometheus target discovery. Do not delete a CNPG PVC to repair a Pod.

docs.title: Project overview
docs.text: Clichy is intended to help users ingest, browse, and manage personal photo collections. The checked-in application currently supports account authentication, photo upload and listing, metadata retrieval, thumbnail derivatives, deletion, and server-side image processing. Similarity primitives exist, but a finished duplicate-review workflow and video support are not evident in the current source.

docs.title: Architecture at a glance
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  Browser -->|HTTPS| Proxy[Cloudflare reverse proxy]
  Proxy --> Tunnel[Cloudflare Tunnel]
  Tunnel -->|HTTP| Ingress[Traefik Ingress]
  Ingress --> Web[React Router web]
  Ingress --> API[Fastify API]
  API -->|CNPG -rw Service| DB[(PostgreSQL primary)]
  DB -->|WAL streaming| Replica[(PostgreSQL standby)]
  API --> FS[(Shared photo filesystem)]
  API --> Redis[(Redis + BullMQ)]
  API --> Worker[Worker]
  Worker --> FS
  Worker --> DB
  Prom[Prometheus] -. scrapes /metrics .-> API

The API and worker mount the photo volume and share originals and derivatives. The API persists upload metadata and an outbox event; a dispatcher publishes queue jobs. The worker computes metadata, hashes, and derivatives.

docs.title: Evaluation notes
docs.text: Key gaps for a demonstration are direct verification of CNPG WAL streaming and failover, the assignment's still-missing database sharding, repeatable Test refresh with anonymization, proof of zero downtime, multi-replica application behavior, Redis availability, and a verified metrics/HPA path. CNPG 1.30 officially supports Kubernetes 1.34–1.36; 1.37 is tested but not officially supported, which matters because the repository's K3s installer targets 1.37. Before marking configured features operational, capture workflow runs, cluster status, Prometheus targets, Headlamp visibility, and a controlled rollout observation.
